source.author: lucan
source.text: Premit inde metus, totumque per agmen Sublimi provectus equo: Quem flagitat, inquit, Vestra diem virtus, finis civilibus armis, Quem quaesistis, adest.
source.text_original: Premit inde metus, totumque per agmen / Sublimi provectus equo: Quem flagitat, inquit, / Vestra diem virtus, finis civilibus armis, / Quem quaesistis, adest.
source.text_english: Then fear presses on them, and he rides through the whole line on his high-mounted horse: The day, he says, that your valor demands, the end of civil arms, the day you have sought, is here.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: ipsum etiam curisque parem talesque prementem corde metus ducit, facilem tamen, Aesona coniunx.
reuse.text_original: ipsum etiam curisque parem talesque prementem / corde metus ducit, facilem tamen, Aesona coniunx.
reuse.text_english: It also leads him to fear himself, equal to his cares and weighing down such fears in his heart, yet tractable, wife of Aeson.
